page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography-focused extensions like AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core testing and small-model LLM prompt processing. In stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, the instance ranks in the top 25%, demonstrating robust computational throughput. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for write operations and cached small-block reads, though large-block uncached read bandwidth falls into the average category. Cryptographic and database operations, including Redis SET execution and Passmark database tests, consistently place in the top 25% of tested hardware.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external Premium Storage. This configuration represents a high resource density for memory-intensive workloads, offering qualitative cost efficiency by avoiding the overhead of local disks for environments that rely on network-attached storage. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive database operations, large-scale web serving, software compilation, and moderate LLM inference tasks.
